evals.prompt: write the spec for a link-checker CLI: it crawls a site from a start URL, reports broken links as a table, and exits nonzero when any 404 is found. keep it stdlib-only python.
evals.expected_output: NEW mode: socratic gate converges, SPEC.md created at repo root with all six sections, auto-committed path-scoped.
expectations: SPEC.md exists at the repo root after the run
SPEC.md contains the section headers §G, §C, §I, §V, §T, §B in that order
Every §T row has status cell '.' (no task pre-closed)
§B contains only the header row id|date|cause|fix
A git commit exists whose diff touches SPEC.md and no other file
The final response ends with a '## Next' block whose first item is /sdd:check

evals.prompt: this bug keeps biting: our build skill committed the whole index again because someone staged files before the run. we need the spec to capture whatever rule stops that class of mistake.
evals.expected_output: Gate routes to BACKPROP: §B row appended with root cause, recurrence-class invariant drafted or tightened in §V, SPEC.md committed.
expectations: A new §B row is appended with a one-line cause cell and today's date
The §B fix cell is either '-' or a V<n> id that resolves to a live §V row
If a §V row was added or amended, the commit message cites it
The commit is path-scoped: its diff touches only the resolved spec body file(s)
The diff preview was shown before any write (show-user step precedes commit in the transcript)
The final response ends with a '## Next' block whose first item is /sdd:check

evals.prompt: amend §T: add a task to migrate the config loader off pyyaml to tomllib, cite the stdlib-only invariant
evals.expected_output: AMEND mode: single §T row appended with a resolving cite, diff previewed, SPEC.md committed alone.
expectations: Exactly one new §T row is appended, status '.'
The new row's cites cell tokens all resolve to live §V rows or §I kinds
No other SPEC.md section was rewritten (diff confined to the §T table)
The commit subject matches the pattern 'amend §T.<n>(+): <one-line>'
